metadata.case_name: LAU CHOI CHUNG v. XIE RENLAN , THE ADMINISTRATRIX OF THE ESTATE OF CHAN WAI KIN, DECEASED AND ANOTHER

source: Apart from “multiple frontal lacerations” (to his forehead/ face), the Plaintiff suffered no other injuries.

injuries.description: Multiple vertical and linear scars on the forehead (with additional small irregular scars adjacent and a bulging soft tissue/dog ear), with scars slightly hypertrophic, irregular edges and mild irregular pigmentation; two pale scars over the left upper eyelid (one an extension from the forehead scar)
source:
“ 1) Multiple vertical and linear scars on the forehead. They extend in front of the hairline towards the left eyebrow. They measure 65 x 2mm, 60 x 2 mm, 40 x 2 mm and 30 x 2 mm respectively. The longest one extends through the medial side of the left eyebrow towards the upper eyelid resulting in patchy loss of hair. The scars are slightly hypertrophic with irregular edges and mild irregular pigmentation. The scars are chronic i.e. soft, non-tender, non-itchy and supple. There is no scar contracture.
2) Multiple small irregular scars adjacent to the linear ones.
3) A bulging soft tissue/ dog ear 10 x 5 mm in the middle of the forehead. The scar becomes more prominent when he looks upwards using the forehead muscles.
4) Two pale scars over the left upper eyelid. The longer one is an extension from the forehead scar. The shorter one 10 x 1 mm, extends from the lower margin of the eyebrow towards the lid margin.
5) There is no scar contracture on the eyebrow or upper eyelid. The movement shape and contour of the eyebrow and eyelid is (sic) normal.”

manifestations.description: post-concussion syndrome (complaints considered compatible with post-concussion syndrome)
slight infection of skin abrasions on forehead (not causing real problem)
visible scarring of forehead and left upper eyelid

treatments_received: Immediate hospitalization at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
Retrieval of about 10 pieces of broken glass from frontal subcutaneous region under local anaesthesia
Out-patient clinic follow-ups at Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Yan Chai Hospital and Polyclinic
Antiseptic cream and antibiotics prescribed by Dr. Shik
treatments_future: Laser resurfacing for scars number 1 and 2 (cost allowed by Court: 45000 HKD)
Surgical treatment for remaining scars (including possible z-plasty or linear closure) (cost allowed by Court: 50000 HKD)

losses.description: The Plaintiff was left with scars (mainly to the forehead); scars are obtrusive and cause concern about appearance.
He felt that his girlfriend left him because of the scarring.
He considered that he would not be able to secure work that required face-to-face contact with customers e.g. being a salesman or a waiter.
